recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not re-generalize condition-related in core and do not restore the old Condition.bodySite extension comment. Future bodySite extension context changes, if any, belong in the FHIR Extension Pack rather than this core checkout.
issue_request: FHIR-31027 asked to generalize the condition-related extension so BodyStructure and Specimen could reference a related Condition. Patient Care published a Not Persuasive with Modification resolution: no new or broadened condition-related extension was needed, the existing bodySite/BodyStructure reference extension should be used, and Condition.bodySite textual comments should be updated while keeping the element named Condition.bodySite.
initial_application: Commit fae49f4994c73b7ac34fc53bde6373fa50928ab4 applied the issue for R5 by adding the J#31027 committee note to Condition.bodySite and changing the comment from old BodySite-resource wording to BodyStructure-oriented extension guidance. Commit c3432543e2b93c3befc06f628938d37e6c1f1f02 later changed the broken extension-bodysite.html link to the canonical bodySite extension URL.
additional_context: FHIR-39630 was later Applied/Persuasive and added Condition.bodyStructure 0..1 Reference(BodyStructure), added con-4 to prevent simultaneous Condition.bodySite and Condition.bodyStructure use, and explicitly resolved to remove the Condition.bodySite comment that referenced the standard extension. The current build scope includes Condition and BodyStructure as active core resources. The condition-related and bodySite extension definitions now live in the FHIR Extension Pack; bodySite remains a BodyStructure reference extension with Condition.bodySite context, and later extension-pack decisions tightened its contexts and added Specimen.collection.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because restoring the old FHIR-31027 extension wording would conflict with the later approved native Condition.bodyStructure model, and broadening condition-related would contradict the original published no-generalization decision.
